objects.description: Asynchronous logging service that buffers log messages in memory and writes them from a dedicated background thread. It is non-copyable, started via start(), and stopped via stop() (also invoked from destructor if still running). Users call append() to queue log lines; internal buffers (FixedBuffer<kLargeBuffer>) are swapped and flushed periodically (flushInterval) and based on roll size. Details of file rolling and actual I/O are not in this header.

objects.definition: typedef detail::AtomicIntegerT<int32_t> AtomicInt32;
objects.description: Alias for AtomicIntegerT specialized for 32-bit signed integers. Provides atomic operations on int32_t.

objects.definition: typedef detail::AtomicIntegerT<int64_t> AtomicInt64;
objects.description: Alias for AtomicIntegerT specialized for 64-bit signed integers. Provides atomic operations on int64_t.

A noncopyable condition variable wrapper in namespace muduo, binding to an external MutexLock. It initializes and destroys an underlying pthread_cond_t and provides wait, timed wait (waitForSeconds), notify, and notifyAll. The Condition must be constructed with a reference to a MutexLock that guards the associated shared state. Waiting temporarily releases the mutex via MutexLock::UnassignGuard. Details of MutexLock, noncopyable, MCHECK, and waitForSeconds implementation are external to this header.

A non-copyable synchronization aid that allows one or more threads to wait until a set of operations being performed in other threads completes. Constructed with an initial count; threads call wait() to block until the count reaches zero; other threads call countDown() to decrement the count. getCount() queries the current count. Internally uses a MutexLock and Condition for thread-safety. Details of noncopyable, MutexLock, Condition, and GUARDED_BY are referenced from other headers and not defined here.

Immutable Gregorian calendar date class storing an internal Julian Day Number. Provides constructors from year-month-day, Julian day number, and struct tm; formatting to ISO string; accessors for year/month/day and weekday; comparison operators. Suitable for value semantics; copyable via muduo::copyable. YearMonthDay is a nested POD used to expose broken-down date components.
Nested POD inside muduo::Date representing a broken-down calendar date (year, month, day). Returned by Date::yearMonthDay() and used for component access.

An exception type in the muduo namespace deriving from std::exception. It stores an error message and a captured stack trace string. Provides what() to retrieve the message and stackTrace() to retrieve the stored backtrace. Constructor takes a message string; destructor is noexcept. Copy and assignment are implicitly allowed. Details of how the stack trace is captured are not shown in this header.

A noncopyable utility class to read small files (up to 64KB). It opens a file provided by filename in the constructor, supports reading either into an internal buffer or into a provided string, and exposes the internal buffer for direct access. Tracks file descriptor, last error, and maintains a fixed-size buffer. Destructor likely closes the file descriptor. Exact error semantics beyond returning errno are not documented here.

A noncopyable, not-thread-safe file appender that opens a file in the constructor and appends data. It buffers writes using an internal 64KB buffer, tracks the total number of bytes written, and provides flush control. Destructor likely flushes and closes the underlying FILE*.

RAII wrapper around zlib's gzFile providing move-only ownership and convenience methods for reading, writing, and querying positions in gzip-compressed files. It closes the gzFile in the destructor. Copying is disabled via noncopyable; movable via move constructor/assignment. Offers factory methods to open files in various modes.

Forward declaration of a file appending helper class in muduo::FileUtil namespace. Only an incomplete type is declared here; its definition is not present in this header. It likely provides buffered append-to-file operations used by LogFile.

Log file manager that appends log lines to a file, periodically flushing and rolling the file based on size and time. Noncopyable. Provides append, flush, and rollFile operations; internal append_unlocked is used when no locking is required. getLogFileName creates a timestamped filename. A tiny formatting helper that stores the result of snprintf-like formatting into an internal 32-byte buffer. Constructed with a printf-style format string and a value of type T; exposes data() and length() for appending to LogStream. Noncopyable is commented out here; class itself has no explicit ownership semantics.

Helper class nested in Logger that stores the basename view of a source file path and its length. Constructible from a string literal or C-string path; trims everything up to the last '/'. Provides lightweight, non-owning pointers to the basename and its size.

The core logging class providing streaming-style logging at various severity levels. It captures source file, line, function, and errno, formats a timestamp, and writes via configurable output/flush callbacks. Usage is primarily through logging macros (LOG_TRACE/DEBUG/INFO/etc.).

Represents process CPU usage times within muduo::ProcessInfo. Holds user and system CPU time counters in seconds, provides a default constructor initializing both to 0.0 and a helper total() to return their sum. Intended to be populated via ProcessInfo::cpuTime().

Lightweight adapter class to accept either const char* or muduo::string arguments and expose a const char* via c_str(). Stores only a pointer; caller must ensure the referenced string outlives the StringArg usage. Copyable and trivial to construct; no ownership or allocation.

Non-owning, lightweight view of a contiguous char buffer. Stores pointer and length; can reference C strings, unsigned char strings, or muduo::string data. Alias for std::string introduced with a using-declaration inside namespace muduo. Serves as the canonical string type for the library.

Resizable network buffer providing prependable, readable, and writable regions. Supports appending, prepending, retrieving, and reading/peeking integers in network byte order. Event-driven reactor core of muduo, one instance per thread. Enumeration controlling the listening socket's SO_REUSEPORT behavior for TcpServer construction. kNoReusePort disables, kReusePort enables. Exact semantics depend on implementation in the source file.

functions.name: muduo::AsyncLogging::AsyncLogging
functions.signature: muduo::AsyncLogging::AsyncLogging(const muduo::string& basename, off_t rollSize, int flushInterval = 3)
functions.description: Constructs an asynchronous logger that buffers log messages in memory and writes them to rolling log files from a background thread. The basename identifies the output log file prefix; rollSize controls log file rollover; flushInterval controls how frequently buffered data is flushed. Typical usage: construct, call start() to launch the background thread, call append() from any thread to enqueue log lines, then call stop() or let the destructor stop the thread.
requirements: basename is used to form output file names; choose a file-system safe name (inferred from common logging patterns).
rollSize should be a positive byte size to enable log file rollover (inferred from parameter name and type).
flushInterval should be non-negative seconds; default is 3 (inferred from common logging patterns).

functions.name: muduo::AsyncLogging::~AsyncLogging
functions.description: Destructor for AsyncLogging. If the logging thread is still running, it calls stop() to flush pending data, notify the background thread, and join it before destruction. Typical usage: either call stop() explicitly during shutdown or rely on the destructor to stop the background thread safely.
requirements: If start() was called, ensure destruction occurs when no further append() calls will be made to this instance (inferred from typical thread-shutdown safety).
Destructor may block while joining the background thread; avoid destroying from contexts where blocking is not allowed (inferred).

functions.name: muduo::AsyncLogging::append
functions.signature: void muduo::AsyncLogging::append(const char* logline, int len)
functions.description: Appends a log record to the in-memory buffers managed by AsyncLogging. The data is queued for the background thread to write to disk according to flush policy and rollover rules. Typical usage: call from any thread to enqueue a pre-formatted log line (including trailing newline if desired).
requirements: logline must be a non-null pointer to a buffer containing at least len bytes.
len must be non-negative and should not exceed the actual buffer length pointed to by logline.
Callers should not modify or free the memory referenced by logline before append() returns (inferred from immediate copy into internal buffers).
For logs to actually be written to files, start() should be called at some point before shutdown (inferred).

functions.name: muduo::AsyncLogging::start
functions.description: Starts the background logging thread and waits until it is fully initialized. After start(), append()ed messages will be processed by the background thread and flushed periodically.
requirements: Should be called at most once per AsyncLogging instance (inferred from internal single Thread member).
May block until the background thread signals readiness (via CountDownLatch). Avoid calling from contexts where blocking is not permitted (inferred).
Call before program shutdown to ensure background processing of appended messages (inferred).

functions.name: muduo::AsyncLogging::stop
functions.description: Stops the background logging thread: signals it to exit, wakes it, and joins the thread, ensuring buffered logs are flushed on shutdown. Intended to be called during program termination; the destructor calls stop() automatically if the logger is still running.
requirements: Blocks until the background thread exits; avoid calling from contexts where blocking is not permitted (inferred).
Should only be called after start() and at most once per instance (inferred from life-cycle semantics).
After stop() returns, do not call append() on this instance (inferred).

functions.name: muduo::detail::AtomicIntegerT::get
functions.description: Atomically reads and returns the current value of the AtomicIntegerT. Implemented with GCC __sync builtins (full barrier semantics; equivalent comment mentions __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST). Typical use: read the latest integer value concurrently updated by other threads.
requirements: The AtomicIntegerT<T> instance must be a valid, constructed object.
May be called concurrently from multiple threads on the same instance.
When T is a signed integer type, callers should avoid relying on wraparound semantics; signed overflow is undefined behavior in C++.
Requires a compiler/platform providing GCC-compatible __sync_* intrinsics (per the header’s implementation).

functions.name: muduo::detail::AtomicIntegerT::getAndAdd
functions.description: Atomically adds x to the current value and returns the value prior to the addition. Implemented with __sync_fetch_and_add (full barrier semantics). Use when you need the previous value while incrementing by an arbitrary delta.
requirements: The AtomicIntegerT<T> instance must be a valid, constructed object.
Argument x must be representable as type T.
May be called concurrently from multiple threads on the same instance.
For signed T, ensure the addition does not overflow/underflow; signed overflow is undefined behavior in C++.
Requires a compiler/platform providing GCC-compatible __sync_* intrinsics.

functions.name: muduo::detail::AtomicIntegerT::addAndGet
functions.description: Atomically adds x to the current value and returns the new value after the addition. Built on getAndAdd.
requirements: The AtomicIntegerT<T> instance must be a valid, constructed object.
Argument x must be representable as type T.
May be called concurrently from multiple threads on the same instance.
For signed T, ensure the addition does not overflow/underflow; signed overflow is undefined behavior in C++.

requirements: The calling thread must hold the associated muduo::MutexLock when calling waitForSeconds() (matching pthread timed wait semantics).

The associated muduo::MutexLock must be valid and correspond to the mutex used to protect the predicate.

functions.name: muduo::LogFile::LogFile

functions.description: Constructs a log file manager that appends log lines to files and rolls them periodically. requirements: Must be called by a thread that currently holds this mutex; otherwise the program will assert/abort in debug builds.
The MutexLock object must be alive.

functions.name: muduo::MutexLock::lock
functions.description: Locks the mutex by calling pthread_mutex_lock and records the owning thread. Blocks until the lock is acquired.
requirements: The MutexLock object must be initialized and alive when called (constructor must have completed).

Must not be called by the same thread if it already holds the mutex (default pthread_mutex_t is non-recursive); doing so may deadlock. (Inferred from use of pthread_mutex_init with default attributes.)
Undefined behavior or deadlock may occur if another thread destroys the mutex while this call is in progress; the object must outlive all lock/unlock operations.
On successful return, the calling thread owns the mutex and must later call unlock() from the same thread.

functions.name: muduo::MutexLock::unlock
functions.description: Unlocks the mutex by clearing the recorded owner and calling pthread_mutex_unlock.
requirements: Must be called only by the thread that currently holds the mutex (ownership is thread-affine).
The MutexLock must be alive and currently locked when called; unlocking an unlocked mutex is an error in pthreads.
After unlock returns, the caller no longer owns the mutex.

requirements: The returned pointer remains valid only as long as the owning MutexLock object remains alive and its internal mutex is not destroyed.
Callers must follow pthreads requirements when using the raw mutex pointer (e.g., lock before pthread_cond_wait as required by POSIX).

Constructing the guard will call mutex.lock(); the mutex must not already be locked by the same thread if the underlying pthread mutex is non-recursive (risk of deadlock).

The constructor must run in the thread intended to own the lock; the same thread will later release it in the destructor.

The associated MutexLock must still be alive when the destructor runs.

Do not attempt to delete or manually free the returned singleton object; ownership is managed internally (either via atexit or intentionally leaked when T::no_destroy exists).

functions.name: muduo::ThreadLocal::ThreadLocal

Typical usage: declare a ThreadLocal<T> at a scope that outlives all threads that will use it, and call value() from each thread to access its own instance.
requirements: T must be a complete type at the point of instantiation (compile-time enforced by sizeof(T) check).

functions.name: muduo::ThreadLocal::~ThreadLocal

Does not directly delete any existing per-thread T instances; those are cleaned up by the registered key destructor when threads exit. Ensure all threads that used this ThreadLocal have finished before destruction to avoid use-after-delete of the key or leaking per-thread objects.
requirements: Destroy ThreadLocal<T> only after all threads that might call value() have stopped using it.

Per POSIX semantics, thread-specific values are destroyed on thread exit via the registered destructor; destroying the key earlier may leave per-thread objects uncollected or cause undefined behavior if threads still access the key.

requirements: May be called from any thread; each thread receives its own T instance.

T must be default-constructible (value() creates a new T() when first accessed from a thread).
T must be a complete type at the point of instantiation (compile-time enforced).

functions.name: muduo::ThreadLocalSingleton<T>::instance

Typical usage: auto& obj = muduo::ThreadLocalSingleton<T>::instance(); Use this when you need one T per thread without manual lifetime management.
requirements: T must be default-constructible (uses new T()).
T must be a complete type at the point of use and destruction (enforced via sizeof(T) check in the destructor).
T must be deletable via operator delete and have an accessible destructor (object is destroyed with delete).
Do not delete or free the returned reference/pointer; lifetime is managed automatically and ends at thread exit.
Calls are thread-specific: each thread gets its own instance; there is no cross-thread sharing.
May throw if T’s constructor throws or allocation fails; callers should be prepared for exceptions in such cases (if using exceptions).
Requires a POSIX threads environment (uses pthread_key_create/pthread_setspecific) and compiler support for thread-local storage (__thread).
Safe to call multiple times in the same thread; returns the same instance each time.

functions.name: muduo::ThreadLocalSingleton<T>::pointer

requirements: May return nullptr if instance() has not been called in the current thread; callers must null-check before dereferencing.
Do not delete or free the returned pointer; lifetime is managed automatically and ends at thread exit.
The pointer is valid only within the calling thread and until that thread exits.
Requires a POSIX threads environment (uses pthread TLS under the hood) and compiler support for thread-local storage (__thread).

functions.name: muduo::net::HttpContext::reset
functions.description: Resets the parsing state to expect a new request and clears the current HttpRequest by swapping with a dummy. Use to reuse the HttpContext for a subsequent request (e.g., persistent connections).
requirements: After reset(), any previous references to the old HttpRequest become invalid and must not be used (inferred from swap/clear semantics).
Should be called only when you are done with the current request and before starting to parse a new one (inferred from purpose).

functions.name: muduo::net::HttpContext::request
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the parsed HttpRequest. Use this accessor to read request method, path, headers, and body without modifying them.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid as long as the HttpContext is alive and not reset() (inferred from reference return and reset semantics).
Typically access after gotAll() is true to ensure a complete request (inferred from parsing workflow).

functions.name: muduo::net::HttpContext::request
functions.description: Returns a mutable reference to the HttpRequest stored in this context. Allows callers to inspect or modify request fields during or after parsing.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid as long as the HttpContext is alive and not reset() (inferred from reference return and reset semantics).
Callers must avoid modifications that break parser expectations if called before gotAll() (e.g., changing method or headers mid-parse) (inferred caution from parsing workflow).

functions.name: muduo::net::HttpRequest::setVersion
functions.description: Sets the HTTP protocol version of this request object. Typical usage is during request parsing, once the version token has been identified.
requirements: May be called at any time; it simply assigns the version enum.
Caller must pass a valid muduo::net::HttpRequest::Version value; unknown values are permitted but will be stored as-is.

functions.name: muduo::net::HttpRequest::getVersion
functions.description: Returns the stored HTTP protocol version for this request.
requirements: No preconditions; callable on a default-constructed object (initially kUnknown).

functions.name: muduo::net::HttpRequest::setMethod
functions.signature: bool muduo::net::HttpRequest::setMethod(const char* start, const char* end)
functions.description: Parses and sets the HTTP method from a character range [start, end). Recognizes GET, POST, HEAD, PUT, DELETE. Returns true if a valid method was recognized and stored; false otherwise.
requirements: Must be called only when the current method is kInvalid; the function asserts (debug builds) that method_ == kInvalid.
start and end must denote a valid contiguous memory range with start <= end; the bytes are treated as a method token (no NUL required).
The range should contain only the method token without trailing or leading spaces for reliable recognition (comparison is exact and case-sensitive).

functions.name: muduo::net::HttpRequest::method
functions.description: Returns the currently stored HTTP method enum value.
requirements: No preconditions; on a default-constructed object this will be kInvalid.

functions.name: muduo::net::HttpRequest::methodString
functions.description: Returns a C-string literal name of the stored method ("GET", "POST", "HEAD", "PUT", "DELETE"), or "UNKNOWN" if the method is not recognized (e.g., still kInvalid).
requirements: No preconditions; returned pointer is to a static string literal and remains valid indefinitely.

functions.name: muduo::net::HttpRequest::setPath
functions.signature: void muduo::net::HttpRequest::setPath(const char* start, const char* end)
functions.description: Sets the request path string from a character range [start, end). Intended to be used during request line parsing.
requirements: start and end must denote a valid readable memory range with start <= end; data need not be NUL-terminated.
The bytes in the range are copied; the source buffer need only be valid for the call duration.

functions.name: muduo::net::HttpRequest::path
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the stored request path.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid as long as the HttpRequest object is alive and its path is not modified.

functions.name: muduo::net::HttpRequest::setQuery
functions.signature: void muduo::net::HttpRequest::setQuery(const char* start, const char* end)
functions.description: Sets the request query string (the portion after '?') from a character range [start, end).
requirements: start and end must denote a valid readable memory range with start <= end; not required to be NUL-terminated.
Content is copied; the source buffer need only be valid for the duration of the call.

functions.name: muduo::net::HttpRequest::query
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the stored query string.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid as long as the HttpRequest object is alive and its query is not modified.

functions.name: muduo::net::HttpRequest::setReceiveTime
functions.description: Sets the timestamp indicating when this request was received.
requirements: Caller must provide a valid muduo::Timestamp value; it is copied into the request.

functions.name: muduo::net::HttpRequest::receiveTime
functions.description: Returns the stored receive timestamp for this request.
requirements: No preconditions; on a default-constructed object this may be the default-constructed Timestamp.

functions.name: muduo::net::HttpRequest::addHeader
functions.signature: void muduo::net::HttpRequest::addHeader(const char* start, const char* colon, const char* end)
functions.description: Parses and adds a header field from a character range representing a single header line split into field name [start, colon) and value [colon+1, end). Leading whitespace after ':' and trailing whitespace at the end of the value are trimmed before storage. If the field already exists, its value is overwritten.
requirements: start, colon, and end must refer to the same contiguous buffer with start <= colon < end.
The memory ranges [start, colon) and (colon, end) must be readable for the duration of the call; data need not be NUL-terminated.
The character at colon is expected to be the ':' separator from an HTTP header line.
Field names and values are treated case-sensitively as stored; no validation of token correctness is performed.

functions.name: muduo::net::HttpRequest::getHeader
functions.description: Looks up and returns a copy of the header value for the given field name. Returns an empty string if the header is not present.
requirements: Field name matching is exact and case-sensitive.
No preconditions; safe to call even if no headers were added.

functions.name: muduo::net::HttpRequest::headers
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the internal map of header fields to values.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid only as long as the HttpRequest object is alive and not modified.
Callers must not attempt to modify the map through this const reference.

functions.name: muduo::net::HttpRequest::swap
functions.description: Swaps all internal state (method, version, path, query, receiveTime, headers) with another HttpRequest instance. Useful for efficient transfers or resetting.
requirements: The referenced object 'that' must be a valid muduo::net::HttpRequest instance; self-swap is safe.
No exceptions are specified; typical use assumes nothrow for primitive swaps, but callers should be prepared for strong exception safety if std::map swap throws in some implementations.

functions.name: muduo::net::HttpResponse::HttpResponse
functions.description: Constructs an HTTP response object with the connection-close flag preset. Use this to create a response and then set status line, headers, and body before serializing it to a Buffer.
requirements: No special constraints on the 'close' argument; either true or false is allowed.
The constructed object should be configured (status code, headers, body as needed) before calling appendToBuffer to serialize it.

functions.name: muduo::net::HttpResponse::setStatusCode
functions.description: Sets the HTTP status code of the response. Typical usage is to assign one of the provided enum values (e.g., k200Ok, k404NotFound) before serialization.
requirements: Argument 'code' should be a valid muduo::net::HttpResponse::HttpStatusCode enum value. 'kUnknown' is technically allowed but may yield an undefined/unknown status line in output.

functions.name: muduo::net::HttpResponse::setStatusMessage
functions.description: Sets the textual reason phrase for the HTTP status line (e.g., "OK", "Not Found"). Call this before serialization if you want a custom reason phrase.
requirements: 'message' can be any string; no specific format is enforced by this interface.

functions.name: muduo::net::HttpResponse::setCloseConnection
functions.description: Controls whether the response indicates the connection should be closed after the response is sent.
requirements: Argument 'on' may be true or false; no additional constraints.

functions.name: muduo::net::HttpResponse::closeConnection
functions.description: Returns the current setting of the connection-close flag for this response. Intended for use when deciding whether to keep the TCP connection alive.
requirements: Callable at any time on a valid HttpResponse instance; no side effects.

functions.name: muduo::net::HttpResponse::setContentType
functions.description: Sets the Content-Type header for the response by delegating to addHeader("Content-Type", contentType).
requirements: 'contentType' may be any string; typically a MIME type (e.g., "text/html; charset=UTF-8"), but no format constraints are enforced here.

functions.name: muduo::net::HttpResponse::addHeader
functions.signature: void muduo::net::HttpResponse::addHeader(const muduo::string& key, const muduo::string& value)
functions.description: Adds or replaces a header field in the response. If the key already exists, its value is overwritten.
requirements: 'key' and 'value' may be any strings. Duplicate keys will result in the last value set being used.
Caller should ensure 'key' is appropriate for an HTTP header field-name if interoperability is required (interface does not enforce this).

functions.name: muduo::net::HttpResponse::setBody
functions.description: Sets the HTTP response body payload. Typically called before serialization.
requirements: 'body' may be any string; no size or encoding constraints are enforced by this interface.

functions.name: muduo::net::HttpResponse::appendToBuffer
functions.description: Serializes the HTTP response (status line, headers, and body) and appends it to the provided Buffer. Intended to be called after configuring status code/message, headers, and body. Exact HTTP version formatting is unspecified in this header (comment notes a future version field).
requirements: 'output' must be a non-null pointer to a valid muduo::net::Buffer instance capable of being appended to.
Should be called after setting desired status, headers, and body to produce a complete response; otherwise defaults (e.g., kUnknown status) will be serialized.

Not documented as thread-safe; callers should avoid concurrent calls from multiple threads (unknown).

functions.description: Starts the HTTP server: binds/listens (via TcpServer) and begins accepting connections and processing HTTP requests using the registered callback.
requirements: setHttpCallback must have been called before start() (explicitly documented).
Should be called after all configuration (e.g., setThreadNum) is done; exact constraints beyond the documented callback requirement are unknown.
Call order: start() should be invoked once per HttpServer instance (typical server lifecycle; exact multiple-call behavior is not documented and is unknown).

functions.name: muduo::net::BufferOutputStream::BufferOutputStream
functions.description: Constructs a ZeroCopyOutputStream wrapper over a muduo::net::Buffer so it can be used as a sink for Protocol Buffers or other zero-copy writers. Records the buffer's initial readable size to compute bytes produced later. The pointer is checked for non-null at construction (CHECK_NOTNULL).
requirements: buf must be non-null; the constructor enforces this via CHECK_NOTNULL (program will abort if null).
buf must point to a valid, initialized muduo::net::Buffer object that remains alive for the entire lifetime of the BufferOutputStream instance (inferred from storing the pointer).
The underlying Buffer will be mutated (write index advanced) as data is written via Next/BackUp.

functions.name: muduo::net::BufferOutputStream::Next
functions.description: Provides a contiguous writable block from the underlying Buffer for zero-copy output. Ensures at least 4096 bytes of writable space, returns a pointer to the current write position and the available byte count, then advances the buffer's write index by that count. Always returns true in this implementation.
requirements: data must be a non-null pointer to a void*; on success *data will be set to a writable memory region owned by the Buffer.
size must be a non-null pointer to int; on success *size will be set to the number of writable bytes (cast from size_t to int).
The caller may write up to, but not beyond, *size bytes to *data before the next call (ZeroCopyOutputStream contract, inferred).
If the caller writes fewer than *size bytes, it must call BackUp(n) with 0 <= n <= *size to return the unused tail before calling Next again (ZeroCopyOutputStream contract, inferred).
The returned pointer becomes invalid after a subsequent call to Next or BackUp (typical ZeroCopyOutputStream contract, inferred).
Because writableBytes() is cast to int, the effective chunk size must fit within the range of int to avoid truncation (inferred from signature and implementation).

functions.name: muduo::net::BufferOutputStream::BackUp
functions.description: Returns unused bytes at the end of the last buffer provided by Next back to the underlying Buffer by moving the write index backward by count bytes.
requirements: Must be called only after a successful Next call that provided the most recent buffer (ZeroCopyOutputStream contract, inferred).
count must be between 0 and the number of bytes returned by the most recent Next that have not already been backed up (ZeroCopyOutputStream contract, inferred).
Do not call BackUp more total bytes than were provided by the last Next; doing so would underflow the write index (inferred from implementation using buffer_->unwrite(count)).

functions.name: muduo::net::BufferOutputStream::ByteCount
functions.description: Returns the total number of bytes produced through this stream since construction, computed as the buffer's current readable byte count minus the initial readable size. Reflects net committed output after considering any BackUp calls.
requirements: None beyond constructing the object; may be called at any time. Returns a non-negative count representing bytes written since construction (inferred from implementation).

functions.name: muduo::net::ProtobufCodecLite::tag
functions.description: Returns the fixed application tag string associated with this codec instance. The tag is prepended to every encoded message and verified on decode to distinguish message families (e.g., "RPC0").
requirements: The ProtobufCodecLite object must have been constructed; tag is immutable after construction.
Returned reference remains valid for the lifetime of the codec object.

functions.name: muduo::net::ProtobufCodecLite::send
functions.signature: void muduo::net::ProtobufCodecLite::send(const muduo::net::TcpConnectionPtr& conn, const ::google::protobuf::Message& message)
functions.description: Serializes the given protobuf message into the wire format (size | tag | payload | checksum) and sends it over the specified Muduo TCP connection.
requirements: conn must refer to a valid, connected TcpConnection; behavior is undefined if the connection is closed or null.
message must be a valid, initialized google::protobuf::Message instance.
The serialized message size must not exceed kMaxMessageLen (64 MiB).
The codec’s tag is included in the framing; peers must expect the same tag.

functions.name: muduo::net::ProtobufCodecLite::onMessage
functions.signature: void muduo::net::ProtobufCodecLite::onMessage(const muduo::net::TcpConnectionPtr& conn, muduo::net::Buffer* buf, muduo::Timestamp receiveTime)
functions.description: Processes bytes in buf using the codec’s wire format, extracting complete protobuf messages. On success it invokes the registered ProtobufMessageCallback (or RawMessageCallback). On errors it invokes the ErrorCallback.
requirements: buf must be non-null and contain data in the codec’s wire format: 4-byte size, tag bytes, payload bytes, 4-byte checksum (adler32 of tag+payload).
Will parse zero or more complete frames; any remaining partial frame bytes are left in buf for a future call.
If a parsed message type does not match prototype_ (by type name), kUnknownMessageType error is reported.
Maximum allowed frame size is kMaxMessageLen; larger sizes result in kInvalidLength.
Checksum must validate; otherwise kCheckSumError is reported.

functions.name: muduo::net::ProtobufCodecLite::parseFromBuffer
functions.description: Parses a protobuf message object from the given raw payload buffer (not including framing). Intended to be overridden for custom parsing; default implementation parses via protobuf reflection.
requirements: message must be non-null and point to an instance of the expected protobuf type.
buf must contain only the protobuf payload (no size, tag, or checksum).
Returns true on successful parse, false on parse failure (kParseError will be used by caller).

functions.name: muduo::net::ProtobufCodecLite::serializeToBuffer
functions.description: Serializes the protobuf message into buf’s internal storage as the raw payload (not including framing). Intended to be overridden for custom serialization; default implementation uses protobuf’s SerializeToArray/Stream.
requirements: buf must be non-null.
message must be a valid, initialized protobuf object according to its required fields.
Returns the number of bytes written on success; negative or zero indicates failure depending on implementation (unknown exact convention).
The total framed size (including tag and checksum) must not exceed kMaxMessageLen.

functions.name: muduo::net::ProtobufCodecLite::errorCodeToString
functions.description: Converts an ErrorCode value to a human-readable string description.
requirements: errorCode must be one of the defined enum values: kNoError, kInvalidLength, kCheckSumError, kInvalidNameLen, kUnknownMessageType, kParseError.
Returned reference refers to a static string valid for the program lifetime.

functions.name: muduo::net::ProtobufCodecLite::parse
functions.signature: muduo::net::ProtobufCodecLite::ErrorCode muduo::net::ProtobufCodecLite::parse(const char* buf, int len, ::google::protobuf::Message* message)
functions.description: Parses a single framed message from the provided contiguous memory region into the given protobuf message object. Intended primarily for unit tests.
requirements: buf must point to a contiguous buffer of length len containing exactly one full frame in the codec’s wire format (size | tag | payload | checksum).
len must be >= kHeaderLen + kChecksumLen + tag().size().
message must be non-null and of a type compatible with the incoming payload; otherwise kUnknownMessageType or kParseError may be returned.
Returns an ErrorCode indicating the first error encountered or kNoError on success.

functions.name: muduo::net::ProtobufCodecLite::fillEmptyBuffer
functions.description: Writes a complete framed message (size | tag | payload | checksum) for the given protobuf message into the provided buffer. Meant to be used before sending or testing.
requirements: buf must be non-null and expected to be empty before the call (function name implies emptiness; behavior if not empty is unspecified).
message must be a valid, initialized protobuf object.
Resulting frame size must not exceed kMaxMessageLen.

functions.name: muduo::net::ProtobufCodecLite::checksum
functions.signature: static int32_t muduo::net::ProtobufCodecLite::checksum(const void* buf, int len)
functions.description: Computes the Adler-32 checksum of the provided memory region. Used for the frame’s checksum over tag+payload.
requirements: If len > 0, buf must be non-null and point to at least len bytes of readable memory.
len must be >= 0.

functions.name: muduo::net::ProtobufCodecLite::validateChecksum
functions.signature: static bool muduo::net::ProtobufCodecLite::validateChecksum(const char* buf, int len)
functions.description: Validates the checksum embedded at the end of a frame against the computed checksum of tag+payload.
requirements: buf must point to a contiguous frame of length len organized as (size | tag | payload | checksum).
len must be at least kChecksumLen plus the lengths of size, tag, and payload; minimally len >= kChecksumLen.
buf must be non-null if len > 0.

functions.name: muduo::net::ProtobufCodecLite::asInt32
functions.description: Interprets the first 4 bytes at buf as a 32-bit signed integer, typically used to read the size field from the frame header.
requirements: buf must point to at least 4 bytes of readable memory.
Assumes the encoding used by the codec (host byte order details are unspecified here; typically network byte order to int32 conversion is performed).

functions.description: Implements google::protobuf::RpcChannel::CallMethod. A valid underlying TCP connection must be set on the channel (via constructor or setConnection) before calling this method (inferred from purpose).
The caller must ensure request and response objects remain alive until the RPC completes and any associated done closure (if provided) is invoked (inferred from pointer ownership semantics).

functions.description: Message callback to process inbound data on the TCP connection. Uses RpcCodec framing to parse RpcMessage instances and dispatch them (either completing outstanding calls or routing to registered services). Intended to be hooked into the connection’s message event.

conn must be a valid TcpConnectionPtr corresponding to the data source (inferred from typical callback usage).

functions.name: muduo::net::RpcServer::RpcServer
functions.description: Constructs an RPC server bound to the given listen address and using the provided EventLoop. Intended to host protobuf-based RPC services over a Muduo TcpServer. Create an instance, optionally configure threads, register services, then call start() to begin accepting connections.
requirements: loop must be a valid, non-null pointer to an EventLoop that remains alive for at least the lifetime of the RpcServer instance (the server uses it internally).
listenAddr must designate a valid local address/port to bind; binding errors are handled by the underlying TcpServer (details not specified here).
Construction does not start listening; callers must invoke start() to begin serving.

functions.name: muduo::net::RpcServer::setThreadNum
functions.description: Sets the number of I/O worker threads used by the underlying TcpServer. Call before start() to configure concurrency.
requirements: numThreads should be a non-negative integer (typical Muduo pattern: 0 means run all I/O in the base EventLoop thread).
Should be called before start() to ensure the thread pool is configured prior to accepting connections (behavior if called after start is unspecified).

functions.name: muduo::net::RpcServer::registerService
functions.description: Registers a protobuf Service with the RPC server so its methods can be exposed over RPC. Services are stored internally and used to dispatch incoming RPC calls. Typically invoked prior to start().
requirements: service must be a valid, non-null pointer to a google::protobuf::Service instance.
The Service object must remain alive and unchanged for at least as long as it is registered with the server (the server stores a raw pointer).
Should be called before start() to ensure the service is available when the server begins accepting requests.
Behavior on duplicate registrations or name collisions is unknown (not specified in this header).

functions.name: muduo::net::RpcServer::start
functions.description: Starts the RPC server, initiating the underlying TcpServer to bind/listen and accept incoming connections. Call after configuring thread count and registering services.
requirements: Should be called once per RpcServer instance to begin serving (idempotency or multiple calls behavior not specified).
Any desired services should be registered via registerService() before calling start().
If setThreadNum() is used, call it before start() so the thread pool is configured prior to accepting connections.

import os

from typing import List

def _rand_str(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int, alphabet: bytes) -> bytes:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return bytes(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))

def _httpish_lines(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Create short log-like or HTTP-like lines to exercise logging/file append paths
    methods = [b"GET", b"POST", b"PUT", b"DELETE", b"HEAD"]
    paths = [b"/", b"/index.html", b"/api/v1/test", b"/long/path/resource", b"/q?q=1"]
    protos = [b"HTTP/1.1", b"HTTP/1.0"]
    hdr_names = [b"Host", b"User-Agent", b"Accept", b"Content-Type", b"X-Custom"]
    agents = [b"curl/7.77.0", b"MuduoFuzzer/1.0", b"Mozilla/5.0"]

    line = b"%s %s %s\r\n" % (
        r.choice(methods), r.choice(paths), r.choice(protos)
    )
    hdrs = []
    for _ in range(r.randint(1, 4)):
        name = r.choice(hdr_names)
        if name == b"User-Agent":
            val = r.choice(agents)
        elif name == b"Accept":
            val = r.choice([b"*/*", b"application/json", b"text/plain"])
        elif name == b"Content-Type":
            val = r.choice([b"text/plain", b"application/octet-stream"])
        elif name == b"Host":
            val = _rand_str(r, 3, 10, b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz") + b".local"
        else:
            val = _rand_str(r, 0, 12, b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789-_.")
        hdrs.append(name + b": " + val + b"\r\n")
    body = b""
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        body = _rand_str(r, 0, 64, bytes(range(32, 127)))
        hdrs.append(b"Content-Length: %d\r\n" % len(body))
    return line + b"".join(hdrs) + b"\r\n" + body

def _protobuf_codec_frame(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build a valid ProtobufCodecLite-like frame: [len][tag+payload][checksum]
    # len = len(tag+payload+checksum), checksum = adler32 over tag+payload (same as zlib.adler32)
    # Use small sizes to keep total under limits.
    import zlib
    tag_len = r.randint(1, 8)
    tag = _rand_str(r, tag_len, tag_len, b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789")
    payload = _rand_str(r, 0, 64, bytes(range(0, 256)))
    body = tag + payload
    checksum = zlib.adler32(body) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    total_len = len(body) + 4
    header = struct.pack("<I", total_len)  # endian is not specified strictly in stub; any consistent works
    frame = header + body + struct.pack("<I", checksum)
    return frame

def _gzip_member(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Return a small valid gzip member
    import zlib
    raw = _rand_str(r, 0, 128, bytes(range(0, 256)))
    c = zlib.compressobj(level=r.randint(1, 6), wbits=16+zlib.MAX_WBITS)  # gzip wrapper
    gz = c.compress(raw) + c.flush()
    return gz

def _loglike_blob(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Create mixed log lines with timestamps and random text
    lines: List[bytes] = []
    n = r.randint(1, 8)
    for _ in range(n):
        ts = r.randint(0, 999999)
        lvl = r.choice([b"TRACE", b"DEBUG", b"INFO", b"WARN", b"ERROR", b"FATAL"])
        msg = _rand_str(r, 0, 40, bytes(range(32, 127)))
        lines.append(b"%s [%06d] %s\n" % (lvl, ts, msg))
    return b"".join(lines)

def _rpc_message_bytes(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Construct a tiny plausible muduo RpcMessage serialized payload using a simple schema-like layout is complex.
    # Instead, provide arbitrary bytes that higher-level fuzz will set via setters; here we keep it small and varied.
    return _rand_str(r, 0, 96, bytes(range(0, 256)))

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose a scenario to feed into FUZZ_PARAM_STR / FILENAME callers.
    choice = r.random()

    chunks: List[bytes] = []
    if choice < 0.20:
        # HTTP-like request lines to exercise parsing paths and logging
        chunks.append(_httpish_lines(r))
    elif choice < 0.35:
        # Protobuf codec framed packet with valid checksum
        chunks.append(_protobuf_codec_frame(r))
    elif choice < 0.50:
        # Gzip member suitable for GzipFile write/read tests
        chunks.append(_gzip_member(r))
    elif choice < 0.70:
        # Log-like multi-line payload
        chunks.append(_loglike_blob(r))
    elif choice < 0.85:
        # Arbitrary binary for RpcMessage request/response setters
        chunks.append(_rpc_message_bytes(r))
    else:
        # Plain random ASCII or binary
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            chunks.append(_rand_str(r, 0, 1024, bytes(range(32,127))))
        else:
            chunks.append(_rand_str(r, 0, 1024, bytes(range(0,256))))

    # Occasionally concatenate multiple chunks to provide broader coverage, staying under 4096 bytes
    while len(chunks) < 3 and r.random() < 0.4:
        add_choice = r.random()
        if add_choice < 0.5:
            chunks.append(b"\n" + _loglike_blob(r))
        else:
            chunks.append(_rand_str(r, 0, 256, bytes(range(0,256))))
        if sum(len(c) for c in chunks) > 4000:
            break

    blob = b"".join(chunks)
    # Ensure size limit
    if len(blob) > 4096:
        blob = blob[:4096]
    return blob

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: arbitrary string
# Goal: Produce interesting, valid std::string payloads to exercise many code paths
# in the provided fuzzing stubs. These strings may be used as filenames, HTTP parts,
# log messages, headers, tags, etc. We generate a variety of structures: ASCII text,
# paths, URLs/queries, HTTP-like lines, numeric strings, binary-ish data with NULs,
# JSON snippets, gzip-like headers, and mixed unicode. Sizes are kept <= 1024 usually,
# and total buffer <= 4096 bytes as required.

ASCII = string.ascii_letters
ALNUM = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
SAFE_HOST = string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "-."
SAFE_PATH = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "/-_.~"
SAFE_QS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_&=.%"


def _rand(r: random.Random, seq: str, n: int) -> str:
    return "".join(r.choice(seq) for _ in range(n))


def _maybe_truncate(s: bytes, maxlen: int) -> bytes:
    return s if len(s) <= maxlen else s[:maxlen]


def _http_request(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    method = r.choice([b"GET", b"POST", b"HEAD", b"PUT", b"DELETE"])  # recognized by HttpRequest
    path_len = r.randint(1, 40)
    path = "/" + _rand(r, SAFE_PATH, path_len)
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        q = _rand(r, SAFE_QS, r.randint(0, 24))
        if q:
            path += "?" + q
    ver = r.choice([b"HTTP/1.1", b"HTTP/1.0"])  # parser knows 1.0/1.1
    host = _rand(r, SAFE_HOST, r.randint(3, 20)) or "localhost"
    ua = _rand(r, ALNUM + "/ .;():", r.randint(5, 24))
    body = b""
    headers = []
    if method in (b"POST", b"PUT") and r.random() < 0.8:
        blen = r.randint(0, 128)
        body = _rand(r, string.printable, blen).encode("utf-8", "ignore")
        headers.append((b"Content-Type", b"application/octet-stream"))
        headers.append((b"Content-Length", str(len(body)).encode()))
    headers.append((b"Host", host.encode()))
    headers.append((b"User-Agent", ua.encode()))
    headers.append((b"Connection", r.choice([b"close", b"keep-alive"])) )
    # Build request
    start = method + b" " + path.encode() + b" " + ver + b"\r\n"
    for k, v in headers:
        start += k + b": " + v + b"\r\n"
    start += b"\r\n" + body
    return start


def _http_header_line(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    key = _rand(r, string.ascii_letters + "-", r.randint(2, 12))
    val = _rand(r, string.printable, r.randint(0, 40))
    return (key + ": " + val + "\r\n").encode()


def _filename(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Used by FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME in other harnesses; here still a string
    parts = []
    depth = r.randint(1, 4)
    for _ in range(depth):
        seg = _rand(r, string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_ .", r.randint(1, 10)).strip()
        if not seg:
            seg = "file"
        parts.append(seg)
    return ("/" + "/".join(parts)).encode()


def _logger_message(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    pieces = [
        b"INFO ",
        _rand(r, ALNUM + " _-:.", r.randint(5, 20)).encode(),
        b" tid=", str(r.randint(1, 1_000_000)).encode(),
        b" val=", str(r.randint(-100000, 100000)).encode(),
    ]
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        pieces.append(b" pi=")
        pieces.append(str(r.random()).encode())
    return b"".join(pieces)


def _json_snippet(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    k1 = _rand(r, ALNUM, r.randint(3, 8))
    k2 = _rand(r, ALNUM, r.randint(3, 8))
    v1 = _rand(r, ALNUM + " _-", r.randint(0, 12))

def _binary_with_nuls(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    n = r.randint(0, 64)
    data = bytearray(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))
    # inject a few NULs
    for _ in range(r.randint(0, 3)):
